skill.name: safe-refactor
skill.description: Refactor in small, verified steps, with behavior locked by tests before any change. Use when asked to refactor, clean up, rename, extract or restructure code without changing behavior.
skill.summary: Preserve existing behavior through characterization tests, small refactoring steps, and verification after every change.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives: inline Markdown command references and a completion report do not establish shell execution or system reconnaissance. A separate rollback instruction could discard pre-existing user edits if git restore is applied without isolating the refactoring changes. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The rollback instruction does not explicitly protect pre-existing user changes.
remediation.suggestion: Record the initial working diff and undo only edits made during the current refactoring step. Require explicit approval before discarding other changes.

semantic_findings.description: The instruction says to undo a failed step using git restore without requiring preservation of existing edits. Restoring an entire modified file could discard unrelated user work.

content.user_title: Refactor Code with Tests at Every Step
content.value_statement: Structural code changes can alter behavior when tests and scope are unclear. This skill guides small refactoring steps with baseline tests, characterization coverage, and repeated verification.
actual_capabilities: Defines refactoring goals and behavior boundaries before editing code.
Locates relevant tests and records baseline results, including existing failures.
Directs characterization tests for code without coverage before structural changes.
Searches callers, dependents, documentation, and configuration for affected names.
Separates renames, extractions, moves, and inlining into independently verified steps.
Reports completed changes, verification results, deferred issues, and uncertain behavior.
limitations: The skill provides workflow instructions, not a standalone refactoring engine.
Behavior preservation depends on test coverage and executable verification.
Unavailable tests, unexplained baseline failures, public API breaks, and discovered bugs require user discussion.
Rollback guidance needs additional safeguards to preserve pre-existing user edits.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Legacy Module
use_cases.description: Add characterization tests before extracting repeated logic while preserving existing outputs and error behavior.

use_cases.title: Rename an Internal Interface
use_cases.description: Find dependent tests, scripts, documentation, and configuration before renaming internal symbols in small verified steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reviewable Structural Changes
use_cases.description: Separate structural improvements from bug fixes and summarize test evidence for each step.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Rename a Local Symbol
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-refactor to rename [symbol] in [file]. Preserve behavior, find references, and run relevant tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: A small internal rename with existing tests

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Extract Repeated Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract duplicated logic from [module]. Record baseline tests, preserve errors and ordering, and verify each extraction separately.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Cover Untested Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [legacy module]. First add characterization tests for current behavior, including edge cases. Keep discovered bugs separate from structural changes.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Refactor Across Modules
prompt_templates.prompt: Restructure [modules] within [scope]. Inventory callers and public APIs. Preserve existing edits, verify each step, and ask before any API break.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate dependent changes across several modules

output_examples.input: Extract repeated validation from a covered module without changing its errors.
output: Goal: remove duplicate validation while preserving error text and validation order.
Changes: extracted shared validation and updated callers in separate steps.
Verification: relevant tests and type checks pass after each step.
Deferred: an existing edge-case bug remains unchanged.

output_examples.input: Reorganize an untested parser while preserving current behavior.
output: Boundary: preserve parsing results, error messages, and input ordering.
Safety net: added characterization tests for normal, empty, and invalid input.
Changes: moved parsing helpers one at a time.
Verification: characterization tests pass after each move.
Uncertainty: behavior outside exercised inputs remains unverified.

best_practices: Define behavior boundaries and record baseline test results before making structural changes.
Preserve pre-existing user edits and undo only changes from the current refactoring step.
Make one kind of change per step and verify it before proceeding.
anti_patterns: Mixing structural cleanup with bug fixes, features, or dependency updates.
Continuing through failing tests without restoring the last verified state.
Renaming public symbols without checking dependents and obtaining approval for breaking changes.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee unchanged behavior?
faq.answer: No. It uses tests and repeated checks to support preservation, but untested behavior can remain uncertain.

faq.question: What happens when the code has no tests?
faq.answer: The workflow calls for characterization tests that capture existing behavior before refactoring begins.

faq.question: Can the refactor include bug fixes?
faq.answer: Discovered bugs should be reported and handled as separate changes, not mixed into the refactor.

faq.question: What happens if tests cannot run?
faq.answer: The skill directs the assistant to stop and ask when tests are unavailable or baseline failures cannot be explained.

faq.question: Can rollback remove my existing edits?
faq.answer: Yes, if git restore is applied too broadly. Require rollback to affect only the assistant's current refactoring changes.
